methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.scenario: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley
signals.signal_reading: A structured community initiative to build AI fluency in Roanoke Valley signals potential distributed capacity-building outside traditional tech hubs, but whether it achieves deep technical capability or shallow platform adoption will determine if it counters or reinforces concentration patterns.

signals.title: Amazon partnership advances AI and cybersecurity education at the Cyber Range - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: Amazon's partnership with Virginia Tech's Cyber Range concentrates advanced AI and cybersecurity training around an established research university, deepening specialized expertise but creating a hub-and-spoke model that may not distribute capability to regions without university anchors.

signals.title: ‘We don’t want it’: Voter backlash against data centers consumes midterm elections
signals.signal_reading: Voter backlash against data centers during elections reveals infrastructure opposition that could prevent both the physical AI infrastructure and the economic spillovers needed for distributed capability development, potentially leaving Virginia with neither concentration benefits nor broad distribution.

signals.title: Wide-ranging symposium to produce undergrad course on AI anxiety - UVA Today
signals.signal_reading: UVA developing an undergraduate course on 'AI anxiety' rather than AI engineering signals educational institutions preparing students for AI-adjacent literacy and ethics rather than deep technical capability, consistent with shallow but potentially broad adoption patterns.

signals.title: Virginia Orders AI Cybersecurity Plan as States Fill Federal Safety Gaps - PYMNTS.com
signals.signal_reading: Virginia's state-level AI cybersecurity mandate concentrates governance expertise in Richmond and likely procurement relationships with NoVA contractors, creating policy-driven concentration rather than distributing security capabilities across regions or building grassroots AI fluency.
